concepts.name: Radian measure
concepts.learningObjective: The student can locate an angle in radians on the unit circle and convert between degrees and radians.

concepts.name: Period of sin(bx) and cos(bx)
concepts.learningObjective: The student can compute the period of y = sin(bx) or cos(bx) and explain why a larger b shortens it.

concepts.name: Amplitude
concepts.learningObjective: The student can read the amplitude from an equation or graph and distinguish it from the peak-to-trough distance.

concepts.name: Solving sin(x) = k on [0, 2π)
concepts.learningObjective: The student can find every solution of a basic sine equation on one period.

title: The Wave-Two Proving Ground

theme.setting: A test dungeon where every wave-2 mechanic has a room

premise: Nine rooms, nine different mechanics. Clear them all.

encounters.prompt: Cross the ridge with your tangent scanner and mark where the terrain is steepest.
hints: The tangent tilts more where the terrain changes height fastest, not where it's highest.
Scan slowly from x = 0 outward and watch how tilted the tangent line gets.
The tangent is tilted furthest from flat somewhere between x = 0 and x = 1.
encounters.wrongFeedback: Steepest means the biggest tilt on the tangent, not the highest point on the ridge.
encounters.debriefLine: A curve's slope changes from point to point: the steepest spot here was x ≈ 0.707.

sourceRef.quote: The derivative measures how steeply a curve rises or falls at each point, and that steepness itself varies along the curve.

encounters.prompt: Apply the same operation to both pans until x stands alone and the chamber unlocks.
hints: Whatever you do to one pan, do to the other, or the scale tips.
Clear the constant off the x side first, then clear its coefficient.
Subtract 5 from both sides, then divide both sides by 3.
encounters.wrongFeedback: Moving a term across the equals sign is really applying the same operation to both sides, and that flips its sign.

sourceRef.quote: Solving 3x + 5 = 20 means applying the same operation to both sides until x stands alone: subtract 5, then divide by 3.

encounters.prompt: Set the coefficients so every atom token balances and the reactor starts.
hints: Balance carbon and hydrogen first; oxygen is easiest to fix last since it appears in both products.
Three carbons and eight hydrogens on the left mean 3 CO2 and 4 H2O on the right.
That makes 10 oxygen atoms needed on the right, so O2 needs a coefficient of 5.
encounters.wrongFeedback: Changing a subscript would make a different substance; only the coefficients out front may change.
encounters.debriefLine: Balanced: 1, 5, 3, 4 (reactants then products) conserves every atom.

sourceRef.quote: Balancing C3H8 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O requires the coefficients 1, 5, 3, and 4 so every carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen atom is conserved.

encounters.prompt: Balance the monthly ledger: every dollar that comes in must be accounted for going out.
hints: Every dollar that enters "Monthly income" has to leave it somehow: rent, bills, or savings.
$2000 comes in and $1400 goes straight to rent and bills, so the rest goes to savings.
Whatever reaches "Savings" with nowhere else to go must leave as the withdrawal.
encounters.wrongFeedback: A budget only balances when every regular expense, not just the big ones, is tracked against income.
encounters.debriefLine: Budget balanced: Transfer to savings = 600, Savings withdrawal = 600.

sourceRef.quote: A budget balances only when every dollar of income is tracked against an expense or a savings transfer.

encounters.prompt: The forge door is carved with mRNA. Translate the codons into the password, one amino acid per codon.
hints: Read three bases at a time; each triplet is one codon.
Look each codon up in the table; the order of the chain follows the order of the codons.
The chain reads: Met Gly Lys Stop
encounters.wrongFeedback: Each codon maps to exactly one amino acid, and the chain keeps the codons' order.
encounters.debriefLine: Translation: 4 codons became the chain Met Gly Lys Stop because each codon codes for one amino acid, not each base.

encounters.prompt: A machine at the bench eats numbers. Watch what it does, then predict its output for 10.
hints: Compare each input with its output: what single step turns one into the other?
The step is the same for every pair; test your guess on all three.
Apply the same step to 10: the machine gives 23.
encounters.wrongFeedback: A function applies the same rule to every input; check your rule against all the pairs the machine showed.
encounters.debriefLine: A function is a rule, not a formula you're told: from 1 → 5, 2 → 7, 5 → 13 you recovered the machine and predicted 23 for 10.

encounters.prompt: The golem's scroll runs these lines. What does it print at the end?

program: if y > 6: x = x + 10 else: x = 0

hints: Run each line in order and write down every container's value as it changes.
a[0] is the FIRST item; lists count from zero.
The scroll prints 4 13.
encounters.wrongFeedback: Trace one line at a time: x = x + 1 is an instruction to update the container, not an equation to solve.
encounters.debriefLine: Variables are containers that change line by line; tracing 6 lines gave 4 13.

encounters.prompt: Runes flash on the enemy's shield. Type each rune's meaning before it fades; missed runes return.

items.prompt: sin θ on the unit circle

hints: Say the definition out loud before you type.
Missed runes come back: use the hint the shield shows.
First rune: y-coordinate
encounters.wrongFeedback: Recognizing a formula isn't the same as recalling it; the runes come back until you can produce each one.
encounters.debriefLine: Rapid recall on 4 trig facts (term → value): retrieval practice, not rereading, is what makes them stick.

encounters.prompt: The Warden's last riddle is a sentence from your notes with one word missing. Fill it.

params.sentence: The value of A stretches the graph vertically but leaves the ___ unchanged.
params.hint: It's the horizontal length of one full cycle.

hints: Read the whole sentence: what could A leave unchanged?
A is the vertical stretch; the missing word is a horizontal property.
The word is period.
encounters.wrongFeedback: Use the surrounding words: 'stretches vertically but leaves … unchanged' points at a horizontal property.
encounters.debriefLine: Cloze: the notes say A leaves the period unchanged, which is exactly why amplitude and period are separate dials.

sourceRef.quote: The value of A stretches the graph vertically but leaves the period unchanged.

intro.text: Nine rooms, nine machines. Show me you can drive them all.

outro.text: Every machine answered to you. Proving ground cleared.

pre.prompt: What is the period of y = sin(3x)?
What is the amplitude of y = -4cos(x)?

post.prompt: What is the period of y = sin(4x)?
What is the amplitude of y = 0.5 cos x?
How many solutions does cos x = 0 have on [0, 2π)?

lessons.bigIdea: Angles measured by arc length on the unit circle; one full turn is 2π.

keyPoints.quote: One complete revolution corresponds to 2π radians.

keyPoints.text: π radians is half a revolution, or 180°.
keyPoints.quote: An angle of π radians corresponds to half a revolution.

watchOut.mistake: π radians is a full circle.
watchOut.fix: π radians is half a circle; a full circle is 2π.

lessons.bigIdea: The horizontal length of one full cycle, 2π/|b|.

keyPoints.text: The period of y = sin(bx) is 2π/|b|.
keyPoints.quote: The period of y = sin(bx) is 2π/|b|.

keyPoints.text: Increasing b makes the graph repeat more often.
keyPoints.quote: Larger values of b compress the graph horizontally.

watchOut.mistake: sin(2x) has period 4π, twice as long as sin(x).
watchOut.fix: A bigger b squeezes the wave, so sin(2x) has period π.

lessons.bigIdea: |A| in y = A·sin(x): the height of the wave above its midline.

keyPoints.text: The amplitude of y = A sin x is |A|.
keyPoints.quote: The amplitude of y = A sin x is |A|.

keyPoints.text: Changing A does not change the period.
keyPoints.quote: The value of A stretches the graph vertically but leaves the period unchanged.

watchOut.mistake: Amplitude is the distance from peak to trough.
watchOut.fix: Peak-to-trough is twice the amplitude; amplitude is |A|.

lessons.bigIdea: Isolate the sine, find the reference angle, then use the quadrants where sine has that sign.

keyPoints.quote: To solve a trigonometric equation, first isolate the trigonometric function.

keyPoints.text: Sine is positive in quadrants I and II.
keyPoints.quote: The sine function is positive in the first and second quadrants.

watchOut.mistake: sin(x) = 1/2 has only one solution on [0, 2π).
watchOut.fix: It has two: π/6 in quadrant I and 5π/6 in quadrant II.
